eli5: A small, cheap computer on one board that runs one program and reads sensors through its pins.
analogy: The line's nervous system: it feels every event and reports it.

eli5: The program we upload to the Arduino; it runs in a loop forever.
analogy: A recipe the cook repeats again and again.

eli5: A metal leg on the Arduino that can read 5 V as HIGH and 0 V as LOW, or switch 5 V on and off.
analogy: A light switch the Arduino can flip or check.

eli5: The two states a digital pin can be in: about 5 V (HIGH) or about 0 V (LOW).
analogy: Lights on or lights off.

eli5: 5 V is the supply voltage; GND (ground) is the 0 V return path every part must also connect to.
analogy: The tap and the drain: water needs both to flow.

eli5: Shines invisible infrared light and notices when something close reflects it back.
analogy: Like an automatic door that opens when you walk up to it.

eli5: Sends a click of sound too high to hear and times the echo to measure distance.
analogy: A bat finding a wall by listening to its own squeak.

eli5: A built-in resistor that holds a pin at HIGH until a button pulls it to GND.
analogy: A spring that keeps a door shut until you push it.

eli5: Ignoring the quick on-off flicker of a switch's metal contacts so one press counts once.
analogy: Waiting for a dropped ball to stop bouncing before you count it as landed.

eli5: A small light; the resistor limits the current so the LED does not burn out.
analogy: A tap reducer that stops a hose from bursting.

eli5: A buzzer with its own tone circuit, so switching on 5 V is enough to make it beep.
analogy: A doorbell that rings by itself once powered.

eli5: A small screen that shows 2 rows of 16 characters.
analogy: A tiny scoreboard at the line.

eli5: A way for chips to talk over just two wires, one for data (SDA) and one for the clock (SCL).
analogy: Two people sharing one walkie-talkie channel and taking turns.

eli5: The number a device answers to on the I2C wires.
analogy: A house number on a shared street.

eli5: A board with hidden metal strips for connecting parts by pushing in wires, no soldering.
analogy: LEGO baseplate for electronics.

eli5: The Arduino sends text to the laptop over the USB cable; the laptop sees it as a port such as COM3.
analogy: A phone line between the Arduino and the laptop.

eli5: How fast serial data is sent, in signal changes per second; 9600 baud is about 960 characters a second.
analogy: The speaking speed both sides agree on.

eli5: A window in the Arduino IDE that shows the text the Arduino sends.
analogy: A peephole into the phone line.

eli5: The free program used to write and upload sketches to the Arduino.
analogy: A word processor for Arduino code.

eli5: A plain text table where each line is a row and commas separate the columns.
analogy: A spreadsheet saved as plain text.

eli5: A Python library that reads and writes the USB serial port.
analogy: The laptop's ear on the phone line.

eli5: A Python library for working with tables of data.
analogy: Excel, but driven by code.

eli5: A Python library that turns a script into a web page with charts and sliders.
analogy: Instant noodles for dashboards: quick and simple.

eli5: GE Vernova's industrial software brand; Rohan's chosen reference for clean front-end design.
analogy: The design 'mood board' we copy the feel of.

eli5: How many parts a station or the line has finished.
analogy: Counting runs in a cricket match.

eli5: Scrapped parts divided by all parts made.
analogy: Out of 10 rotis, how many got burnt.

eli5: How long one station works on one part, not counting time spent waiting for work.
analogy: How long the barber actually spends on one haircut.

eli5: How long one part takes from entering the line to leaving it, including waiting.
analogy: Your total time at the barber's, queue included.

eli5: Available time divided by customer demand: the pace the line must keep.
analogy: A metronome that sets the beat the line must follow.

eli5: Good parts made per unit of time.
analogy: Litres per minute coming out of a tap.

eli5: The one step that limits how fast the whole line can make good parts.
analogy: The narrow neck of a bottle that sets how fast water pours.

eli5: When the old bottleneck is fixed and another step becomes the slowest.
analogy: Unblock one lane of traffic and the jam moves to the next junction.

eli5: The idea that every system has one constraint that limits it, and you improve the system by improving that constraint first.
analogy: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.

eli5: Parts that have entered the line but not yet left it.
analogy: Clothes that are washed but not yet dried and folded.

eli5: Parts waiting in front of a station because it cannot keep up.
analogy: A queue at a single ticket counter.

eli5: A station sits idle because no parts are reaching it.
analogy: A cashier with no customers.

eli5: A station cannot pass its finished part on because the next step is full or stopped.
analogy: A waiter holding plates because the table is not ready.

eli5: Time the line is stopped, logged with a reason (B breakdown, M no material).
analogy: Minutes a shop is shut during opening hours.

eli5: One score: availability × performance × quality.
analogy: A report-card grade combining attendance, speed and accuracy.

eli5: Run time divided by planned time.
analogy: Attendance: how much of the lesson you were present for.

eli5: How fast the line ran compared with its ideal cycle time.
analogy: Speed: how many questions you answered in the time you were there.

eli5: Good parts divided by all parts made.
analogy: Accuracy: how many answers were right.

eli5: Our approximate OEE, because the ideal cycle time is our own estimate.
analogy: A rough grade before the official marks come out.

eli5: Average WIP = throughput × average flow time.
analogy: More people in the queue means a longer wait if the counter's speed stays the same.

eli5: A fixed limit on how many parts may be inside the line; a new part enters only when one leaves.
analogy: A club that lets one person in only when one comes out.

eli5: Moving work between stations so they take about the same time.
analogy: Sharing the bags so every hiker carries a similar load.

eli5: Material kept in stock waiting to be used, here the parts in the raw-material bin.
analogy: The rice in your kitchen jar.

eli5: The stock level at which you refill, so you do not run out while the refill arrives.
analogy: Buying milk when one packet is left, not when it's gone.

eli5: A little extra stock kept for surprises.
analogy: A spare pen in your pencil box.

eli5: A signal light that tells everyone on the floor about a problem straight away.
analogy: A traffic light for the line.

eli5: A number used to judge how well something is going.
analogy: Your CGPA.

eli5: Parts are handled in the order they arrived.
analogy: A bus queue.

eli5: An average where each value counts for as long as it lasted.
analogy: Average speed on a trip: an hour at 60 counts more than a minute at 100.

eli5: Public data from a real Bosch production line, shared on the Kaggle website in 2016.
analogy: A real factory's diary, made public.
